places.name: Università degli Studi di Firenze (Rectorate & Humanities)
places.description: Florence's public research university, tracing its origins to the Studium Generale of 1321 and formally established as a university in 1924. Its historic rectorate on Piazza San Marco anchors a network of schools spread across the city, from humanities in the centro storico to medicine at Careggi. It is one of Italy's largest and most productive research universities.
places.demographics: Mostly Italian undergraduates and graduate students; roughly 10% international, plus Erasmus exchange students

places.name: Università di Firenze – Novoli Social Sciences Campus
places.description: The University of Florence's modern social-sciences campus, opened in 2004 in the redeveloped Novoli district on the site of the former FIAT factory. It gathers the schools of Law, Economics and Political Science around a contemporary quad and the D'Ancona-designed university park.
places.students: About 15,000 enrolled across the three schools
places.demographics: Predominantly Italian students, with Erasmus and international exchange students

places.name: European University Institute
places.address: Badia Fiesolana, Via dei Roccettini 9, 50014 San Domenico di Fiesole (FI)
places.description: An intergovernmental doctoral and postdoctoral institute created by the European Community, welcoming its first researchers in 1976. From the hillside Badia Fiesolana and surrounding villas it grants PhDs in economics, law, history and political science and hosts the Robert Schuman Centre and the Historical Archives of the European Union.
programs: PhD in Political and Social Sciences
LLM in Comparative, European and International Laws
School of Transnational Governance master's and executive training
places.students: About 600 doctoral researchers plus roughly 300 fellows and master's students
places.demographics: Graduate researchers from all EU member states and beyond; highly international, all-postgraduate community

places.name: Accademia di Belle Arti di Firenze
places.description: Italy's state fine-arts academy in Florence, refounded by Grand Duke Pietro Leopoldo in 1784 and descended from Vasari's 1563 Accademia delle Arti del Disegno — the first art academy in Europe. It shares a building with the Galleria dell'Accademia, home of Michelangelo's David, and grants degrees equivalent to university diplomas.
places.demographics: Mix of Italian students and a large international contingent, notably from China and other non-EU countries

places.name: Conservatorio di Musica Luigi Cherubini
places.description: Florence's state music conservatory, founded in 1849 and named for the Florentine composer Luigi Cherubini. Steps from Piazza San Marco, it trains musicians at bachelor's and master's level and holds an important collection of historical instruments, including pieces by Stradivari from the Medici court.
places.demographics: Mainly Italian music students with a growing international enrollment, especially from Asia

places.name: Polimoda International Institute of Fashion Design & Marketing
places.description: One of the world's top-ranked independent fashion schools, founded in 1986 with backing from the city of Florence and originally in partnership with FIT New York. Headquartered in the 19th-century Villa Favard on the Arno, with design labs at the Manifattura Tabacchi complex, it feeds talent directly into the Florentine and global luxury industry.
places.demographics: Roughly 70% international students from over 70 countries; undergraduate and master's level

places.name: IED – Istituto Europeo di Design, Firenze
places.description: The Florence branch of Italy's largest private design education group, founded in Milan in 1966. Steps from the Duomo, IED Firenze focuses on fashion, accessories and luxury goods, with additional spaces in Palazzo Pucci for its fashion department.
programs: Semester and summer courses in design and fashion
places.demographics: Mixed Italian and international students; undergraduate-level three-year courses plus short programs

places.name: Istituto Marangoni – The School of Fashion & Art, Firenze
places.description: The Florence campus of the storied Milanese fashion school founded in 1935, opened in 2016 in a historic palazzo on Via de' Tornabuoni, the city's luxury shopping street. The school specializes in fashion styling, design and the art business, drawing on Florence's museums, ateliers and leather-goods industry.
places.demographics: Strongly international student body at undergraduate and master's level

places.name: Accademia Italiana – Arte, Moda e Design
places.description: A private academy of art, fashion and design founded in 1984, occupying the Temple Leader building directly on Piazza Pitti. It grants accredited bachelor's and master's degrees and has long welcomed both Italian and international students, with a rooftop loggia overlooking the Pitti Palace.
places.demographics: Mixed Italian and international students; also hosts US study-abroad semester students

places.name: LABA – Libera Accademia di Belle Arti Firenze
places.address: Piazza di Badia a Ripoli 1/A, 50126 Firenze
places.description: A legally recognized private fine-arts academy in the Badia a Ripoli district, granting AFAM degrees equivalent to university diplomas. LABA emphasizes contemporary creative industries, from photography and graphic design to fashion and cinema.
places.demographics: Mostly Italian undergraduates, with some international students

places.name: SACI – Studio Arts College International
places.address: Palazzo dei Cartelloni, Via Sant'Antonino 11, 50123 Firenze
places.description: A US-accredited (NASAD) studio art college founded in 1975, housed in the Baroque Palazzo dei Cartelloni near San Lorenzo. SACI offers studio art, design and conservation courses for study-abroad students and grants MFA degrees, with galleries that host regular exhibitions open to the public.
places.demographics: Mostly US undergraduates on semester programs plus small MFA and post-bac cohorts

places.name: Santa Reparata International School of Art
places.description: An American-style art school founded in 1970 as a printmaking workshop, now spread across several sites around Via San Gallo in the historic center. SRISA offers studio art, design and liberal arts courses to visiting university students and partners with Maryville University as its US school of record.
places.demographics: Mostly US study-abroad undergraduates, with some independent international students

places.name: The Florence Academy of Art
places.description: Founded in 1991 by American painter Daniel Graves, this atelier revived rigorous 19th-century academic training in drawing, painting and sculpture. Now housed in a converted 19th-century customs house east of the center, it is the flagship of the international classical-realist movement, with sister campuses in the US and Sweden.
places.demographics: Adult students from around 30 countries, largely from the US and northern Europe

places.name: Angel Academy of Art
places.description: A private atelier founded in 1997 by Michael John Angel, a pupil of Pietro Annigoni, teaching old-master drawing and painting methods. Its three-year diploma program uses sight-size and classical techniques in the tradition of the 19th-century academies.
programs: Three-year Diploma in Drawing and Painting
places.demographics: Small international cohort of adult students, many from the US, UK and northern Europe

places.name: Charles H. Cecil Studios
places.description: An intimate portrait-painting atelier in a former church in the San Frediano quarter of the Oltrarno, led by American painter Charles Cecil. Successor to the Cecil-Graves studio, it teaches the sight-size method in studios once used by 19th-century sculptors, training a small number of dedicated painters each year.
programs: Full-time atelier training in drawing and oil painting
places.demographics: Small international group of adult students, predominantly American and British

places.name: Fondazione Studio Marangoni
places.description: Florence's center for contemporary photography, founded by photographer Martino Marangoni, with classrooms, darkrooms and an exhibition gallery on Via San Zanobi. It runs a three-year photography program and hosts exchange students from US universities including NYU Tisch.
places.demographics: Mix of Italian and international photography students

places.name: Palazzo Spinelli – Istituto per l'Arte e il Restauro
places.description: A renowned institute for art restoration and conservation founded in 1976, based in the Renaissance Palazzo Spinelli near Santa Croce. It trains restorers of paintings, frescoes, paper, ceramics and furniture, and has restored thousands of artworks including flood-damaged pieces from 1966.
programs: Restoration of ceramics, wood and stone
places.demographics: Italian and international students, including many US and Asian trainees on professional courses

places.name: Scuola di Musica di Fiesole
places.address: Villa La Torraccia, Via delle Fontanelle 24, 50014 San Domenico di Fiesole (FI)
places.description: One of Italy's most prestigious music schools, founded in 1974 by violist Piero Farulli of the Quartetto Italiano and housed in Villa La Torraccia near San Domenico. It teaches everyone from toddlers to professionals, grants accredited higher-education music degrees, and is home to the celebrated Orchestra Giovanile Italiana.
programs: Instrumental and vocal training at all levels
Accredited AFAM bachelor's and master's degrees
places.demographics: Mostly Italian students from children to conservatory-level; advanced courses draw students from across Italy and abroad

places.name: Istituto Lorenzo de' Medici (LdM) / Marist Italy
places.description: Founded in 1973, LdM is one of Italy's largest international education institutions, occupying a former convent complex near San Lorenzo. Since 2006 it has served as the Florence branch campus of Marist University, whose students can complete full four-year US bachelor's degrees here alongside thousands of semester study-abroad visitors from dozens of partner universities.
programs: Semester and summer study abroad in liberal arts
Marist bachelor's degrees (Studio Art, Art History, Fashion Design, Digital Media, Interior Design, Italian, Conservation)
places.demographics: Mostly US undergraduates on semester programs, plus degree-seeking students from many countries

places.name: Florence University of the Arts – The American University of Florence
places.description: A private American-model institution whose schools span hospitality, food and wine (Apicius), fine arts, fashion and liberal arts, with teaching sites clustered near Santa Croce. FUA-AUF pioneered 'community engagement' learning through student-run venues like the Fedora pastry shop and Ganzo restaurant, and partners with Fairfield University as its school of record.
places.demographics: Predominantly US study-abroad undergraduates, with international certificate students

places.name: The British Institute of Florence
places.description: Founded in 1917, this is the oldest British cultural institute abroad, teaching Italian to foreigners and English to Italians from Palazzo dello Strozzino. Its Harold Acton Library on the Lungarno Guicciardini holds the largest collection of English-language books in Italy and hosts a beloved weekly lecture series.
places.students: Several thousand course enrollments per year
places.demographics: International adults learning Italian and Florentines learning English; also hosts visiting university groups

places.name: Scuola Leonardo da Vinci – Firenze
places.description: The Florence seat of one of Italy's best-known Italian-language school networks, teaching since 1977 just two blocks from the Duomo. Alongside intensive Italian courses it offers exam preparation, cultural electives and professional courses in fashion, art and cuisine.
programs: Italian plus art, cooking or fashion electives
places.demographics: International students of all ages from over 90 countries on short- and long-term courses

places.name: Linguaviva
places.description: A family-run Italian language school founded in the 1970s, located in an elegant palazzina near Santa Maria Novella station. Linguaviva is accredited for university foundation programs and pathways into Italian universities and art academies.
programs: Italian for art and design school admission
places.demographics: International students, many preparing for Italian university or academy admission

places.name: Centro Machiavelli
places.description: An intimate Italian language and culture school on Piazza Santo Spirito, teaching since 1978 in the heart of the artisan Oltrarno. Its trademark is combining language classes with craft internships in Florentine workshops, from bookbinding to mosaics.
places.demographics: Adult international learners from Europe, the Americas and Asia

places.name: Europass Italian Language School
places.description: An Italian language school in the neoclassical Palazzo Galletti, a short walk from the Duomo, also known for its large teacher-training academy. It offers intensive Italian, exam preparation and cultural courses year-round.
places.demographics: Adult international learners and visiting European teachers on Erasmus+ mobility

places.name: Istituto Europeo
places.description: A language, music and culture school on the corner of Via de' Tornabuoni in the heart of Florence. Beyond Italian language courses it is known for opera, voice and instrumental music programs and university-partnered study-abroad offerings.
places.demographics: International students, including US study-abroad groups and music students

places.name: NYU Florence – Villa La Pietra
places.address: Villa La Pietra, Via Bolognese 120, 50139 Firenze
places.description: New York University's Florence campus occupies the 57-acre Villa La Pietra estate on a hill north of the city, bequeathed to NYU by Sir Harold Acton in 1994. Students live and study among five historic villas, Renaissance-style gardens and one of the finest private art collections in Italy.
programs: Liberal arts semester and year programs
places.demographics: Mostly NYU undergraduates including a first-year cohort; visiting students from other US universities also admitted

places.name: Syracuse University Florence
places.description: Established in 1959, Syracuse Florence is the oldest continuously operating American university program in Florence and one of the largest, centered on the Villa Rossa on Piazza Savonarola. Its architecture, art and liberal-arts curriculum is supplemented by studios and the Villa Rossa garden classrooms.
places.demographics: Mostly US undergraduates from Syracuse and partner universities on semester programs

places.name: Kent State University Florence
places.address: Palazzo Vettori, Via Camillo Cavour 26, 50129 Firenze
places.description: Kent State has taught in Florence for over 50 years, beginning with its architecture program in the early 1970s. Since 2016 the campus has occupied Palazzo Vettori at the corner of Via Cavour and Via degli Alfani, near the Duomo, hosting architecture, fashion and liberal-arts students year round.
places.demographics: US undergraduates, primarily from Kent State's Ohio campuses

places.name: Gonzaga in Florence
places.description: Gonzaga University's flagship study-abroad program, running in Florence since 1963 — one of the longest-standing American programs in Italy. Its center near Piazza San Marco serves a tight-knit cohort each semester with a Jesuit liberal-arts curriculum and extensive travel components.
programs: Liberal arts semester and year programs
places.demographics: Mostly Gonzaga undergraduates, largely sophomores and juniors

places.name: Pepperdine University Florence Program
places.description: Seaver College's residential Florence house sits on Viale Milton along the Mugnone stream, a short walk from the historic center and Santa Maria Novella station. Students live and take classes together in the villa-style program house, following Pepperdine's faith-based liberal arts curriculum with extensive field trips.
programs: Liberal arts academic year and semester programs
places.demographics: Pepperdine undergraduates, mostly sophomores, living in a single residential program house

places.name: Stanford University – Breyer Center for Overseas Studies in Florence
places.address: Palazzo Capponi alle Rovinate, Via de' Bardi 36, 50125 Firenze
places.description: Stanford first opened a Florence campus in 1960, and its Bing Overseas Studies Program now operates from the medieval Palazzo Capponi alle Rovinate on the Oltrarno bank of the Arno. Small quarterly cohorts take Stanford courses in the humanities, social sciences and Italian culture with local internships and field trips.
places.demographics: Stanford undergraduates on quarter-long rotations

places.name: James Madison University – Florence Programs (Palazzo Capponi)
places.address: Palazzo Capponi, Via de' Michelozzi 2, 50125 Firenze
places.description: JMU runs its European center from the 16th-century Palazzo Capponi in the Santo Spirito quarter, housing classrooms, a library and a student residence. It hosts the undergraduate Semester in Florence as well as a one-year M.A. in Political Science focused on European Union policy studies.
programs: M.A. in Political Science: European Union Policy Studies
places.demographics: JMU undergraduates plus a small international graduate cohort

places.name: Richmond American University London – Florence Study Center
places.description: The Italian study center of Richmond, the American university in London, occupying the Renaissance Palazzo Michelozzi on Via Maggio near the Ponte Vecchio. The center specializes in studio and fine arts, art history and Italian culture for semester students, including AIFS program participants.
places.demographics: US and international undergraduates from Richmond London and AIFS partner universities

places.name: Fairfield University Florence Campus
places.description: Fairfield University opened its dedicated Florence campus in 2019 in the Santa Croce district, operated in partnership with Florence University of the Arts, for which Fairfield serves as US school of record. The Jesuit university's students take liberal-arts, business and nursing courses alongside FUA's experiential programs.
places.demographics: Mostly Fairfield undergraduates on semester programs

places.name: Florida State University – Florence Study Center
places.description: One of the oldest US programs in the city, Florida State has taught in Florence since 1966 and today operates a study center on Via dei Neri between the Uffizi and Santa Croce. FSU offers full academic-year, semester and summer terms, including a popular first-year-abroad option.
programs: Liberal arts semester and year programs
places.students: Several hundred per year including large summer terms
places.demographics: Florida State undergraduates, including first-year students spending their freshman year abroad

places.name: California State University – International Programs Florence Center
places.description: The systemwide California State University International Programs center, occupying two floors of a 19th-century palazzo near Piazza Beccaria. CSU students from across the 23-campus system spend a full academic year here, with options to study architecture and design or enroll directly in Italian institutions.
programs: Full academic year liberal arts program
places.demographics: California State University undergraduates on a year-long program

places.name: ISI Florence – International Studies Institute at Palazzo Rucellai
places.address: Palazzo Rucellai, Via della Vigna Nuova 18, 50123 Firenze
places.description: An independent American study-abroad institute founded in 2001, headquartered on the piano nobile of Leon Battista Alberti's landmark Palazzo Rucellai, with a second seat in Palazzo Bargagli on the Arno. ISI hosts semester programs for numerous US partner universities in the liberal arts, architecture and business.
places.demographics: US undergraduates from partner universities such as Penn State, Rutgers and Villanova

places.name: CET Academic Programs – Florence Center
places.description: CET's Florence center sits in the San Niccolò quarter of the Oltrarno, steps from the Arno near Ponte alle Grazie. Its semester programs pair US undergraduates with Italian student roommates and emphasize art conservation, sustainability and Italian studies.
places.demographics: US undergraduates from many home universities, housed with Italian roommates

places.name: Harding University in Florence (HUF)
places.address: Villa Il Palazzaccio, Via di Triozzi 57, 50018 Scandicci (FI)
places.description: Harding University's first international program, launched in 1980 and based since 1984 in a 15th-century hillside villa in Scandicci, southwest of Florence. Cohorts of up to 35 students live, study and travel together each semester in this residential Christian liberal-arts program overlooking the Arno valley.
programs: Group travel across Italy and Europe
places.students: Up to 35 per semester, three terms per year
places.demographics: Harding University undergraduates in a residential villa program

places.name: Sarah Lawrence College in Florence
places.address: Palazzo Spinelli, Borgo Santa Croce 10, 50122 Firenze
places.description: A small, deeply immersive year and semester program run from offices in Palazzo Spinelli near Santa Croce. True to Sarah Lawrence's seminar model, students take individual tutorials, enroll in University of Florence courses and live with Florentine families or in apartments.
programs: Year and semester liberal arts program
places.demographics: Sarah Lawrence and visiting US undergraduates with strong Italian preparation

places.name: Smith College – Junior Year Abroad in Florence
places.description: Smith College has sent students to Florence since 1931, making it one of the oldest junior-year-abroad programs in Italy. From its center on Via Giusti, students take Smith seminars, enroll at the University of Florence and live with local host families for full linguistic immersion.
places.demographics: Smith College students and Five College/consortium women undergraduates with Italian language preparation

places.name: Middlebury College School in Italy – Florence Sede
places.description: Middlebury's language-pledge Florence school, where students commit to speaking only Italian, direct-enroll at the University of Florence and other local institutions, and live with Italian hosts. The sede on Via Pier Capponi supports both undergraduates and graduate students of the Italian School.
programs: Semester and year immersion with language pledge
places.demographics: US undergraduates and graduate students with advanced Italian; full immersion model

places.name: CEA CAPA Education Abroad – Florence Center
places.description: The Florence center of one of the largest US study-abroad providers, located directly on Piazza della Repubblica in the heart of the city. CEA CAPA offers semester, summer and internship programs with credit transcripted through the University of New Haven.
programs: Liberal arts and business semester programs
places.demographics: US undergraduates from a wide range of home universities

places.name: ACCENT Global Learning – Florence Study Center
places.description: ACCENT's Florence Study Center fills a four-story historic palazzo on Via Sant'Egidio, five minutes from the Duomo, with classrooms, a gallery, library and garden. It hosts more than 25 customized university-branded programs each year for partners including UC Education Abroad, the University of Minnesota and Michigan State.
programs: Customized university semester and summer programs
places.students: Several hundred per year across partner programs
places.demographics: US undergraduates on university-branded custom programs (UCEAP, Minnesota, TCU, MSU and others)

places.name: Georgetown University – Villa Le Balze
places.description: Georgetown's study center occupies a 1912 Cecil Pinsent-designed villa and terraced gardens clinging to the Fiesole hillside, given to the university in 1979 by the Rockefeller family. Small cohorts live and study on site with sweeping views over Florence, running programs since 1981.
places.demographics: Georgetown undergraduates plus some visiting US students
